title: The Pipeline Is Dead - Iris ten Teije, Sky Valley Ambient Computing
talk_summary: A vision talk arguing that cheap AI code generation dissolves the frozen-artifact CI/CD pipeline in favor of a canonical 'stem' plus bounded, per-user divergences. The genuinely transferable content is the architecture of bounded, isolated, reversible variants with provenance and intent-level merging, not the per-user product thesis.

takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of one tangled artifact, they run a canonical stem plus divergences that are bounded, isolated, and individually reversible, so a bad variant cannot corrupt the stem or reach another user.
takeaways.evidence_quote: The divergences are bounded, isolated, and individually reversible. A bad variant can silently corrupt the stem or reach another user.

takeaways.what_they_do: Developers declare what can and cannot be adapted (e.g., payment/off-limits fields), so automated changes are only permitted inside an explicit safe envelope.
When many variants exist, they don't force everyone onto the same commit; they converge on the same goal through different paths, merging intent/outcome rather than code.
takeaways.evidence_quote: don't merge code, merge intent, merge outcome

takeaways.what_they_do: They separate 'is the change correct' from 'is the change desirable' (did it actually improve a tracked metric like retention or support tickets).
takeaways.evidence_quote: anyone can make a code change now, but the hard part is knowing whether you actually found an improvement, an uplift

takeaways.what_they_do: With no single artifact, they treat software as stem plus immutable divergences and trace any version back to the signal and exact adaptation that produced it, via graph query instead of a version number.
takeaways.evidence_quote: every divergence is immutable, inspectable, attributable

takeaways.what_they_do: They argue calling a model to write code is commoditized; the business value is in observability, validation, and coordination around it.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Generation has become easy... The other part, observability, validation, coordination, that is the entire business.
